Tim Hawkins, statement carried May 25→26): 'U.S. forces conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran today to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces… continues to defend our forces while using restraint during the ongoing ceasefire.' IRGC claim: 1× MQ-9 shot down + 'fired upon' 2nd MQ-9, RQ-4 Global Hawk, F-35 'forcing them to retreat' — US official to NBC News/Fox: 'no US aircraft were hit'; CENTCOM silent on platform losses; if confirmed, 25th MQ-9 lost in war. They're going to be open one way or the other.' Iranian delegation in Doha for ceasefire-extension talks; 60-day MOU + Hormuz reopening framework holds. Baghaei: 'We have reached conclusions on a large portion of the issues, but no one can claim that the signing of an agreement is imminent.' IRAN INTERNET PARTIAL RESTORATION on Day 88 after 87 days — NetBlocks (per UPI): 'partial restoration to Internet connectivity in #Iran on day 88, after 2,093 hours of near-total isolation from international networks, the longest nationwide Internet shutdown in modern history'; 1st VP Aref: 'the first step toward free and regulated access to cyberspace has been taken'; decision taken May 25 at Supreme Council of Cyberspace. LEBANON: IDF airstrike on Mashghara village (Bekaa Valley) late May 25/overnight killed 11 (Lebanese MoH) / 12 (state NNA / AP, 12 bodies pulled from rubble) including a woman and two girls (Lebanese MoH via Antiwar.com). Al Jazeera correspondent Zeina Khodr: 'at least 10 attacks in the span of half an hour on an area with residential buildings.' Part of 76 IDF airstrikes on Lebanon May 25 (Antiwar.com). Netanyahu authorized intensified Hezbollah operations after Hezbollah drone killed IDF reservist Staff Sgt. Noam Hamburger; US Amb. Huckabee approved expansion but warned Israel 'not to bring down buildings in Beirut' (Channel 12). Lebanon/Israel direct military talks set for May 29 in Washington. Lebanese MoH X post May 26: 34 killed in past 24h — implied cumulative ~3,219 (FLAG: dashboard cumulative still 3,185 pending reconciliation). MARKETS: S&P 500 +0.61% to record 7,519.12 (45.65 pts); Nasdaq +1.19% to record 26,656.18; Dow -0.23% to 50,461.68 (-118.02 pts); Russell 2000 2,869.23; VIX 16.59. Rally led by Micron +19% — UBS hiked PT, market cap topped $1T for first time (+200% YTD, +800% past 12 months); semiconductor surge (AMD +6%, On Semi +9%, Western Digital +9%, SMH ETF 52-wk high +3%). Polymarket May 26: 91% probability S&P opens higher — resolved Yes. The Conference Board (May 26 release) Consumer Confidence 93.1 (-0.7 from upwardly revised 93.8; survey May 1–19); Chief Economist Dana M. Peterson: 'Consumer confidence edged downward in May as the inflationary impacts of the war in the Middle East intensified… References to prices and oil and gas increased in frequency for a second consecutive month, while mentions of war, geopolitics, and conflict remained elevated.' LNW CIO Ron Albahary (CNBC): investors 'pathologically optimistic.' OIL: Brent (ICE Jul'26) settle $99.58 (+3.58%, +$3.43) on strikes; WTI (NYMEX Jul'26) settle $93.89 (-2.81% vs Friday May 22 $96.60, no Monday settle due to Memorial Day); Brent-WTI spread widened to $5.69. AAA national gas $4.491 (-1.6¢ d/d), GasBuddy $4.45 (-6.6¢ w/w); diesel $5.571. Patrick De Haan: 'Average gasoline prices declined in 40 states over the last week as falling oil prices helped offset earlier price cycling… Much of the decline came after renewed optimism surrounding a potential U.S.-Iran agreement pushed oil prices lower.' HORMUZ: IRGC Navy claim (Mehr) 25 vessels coordinated May 26 (~25% of ~100/day Kpler baseline); US Navy reportedly resumed escorting tankers per Trading Economics. Cumulative range: Pentagon $29B → Semler/SPRI $71.8B → Watson/Brown $40B in consumer fuel ALONE. Trump Cabinet meeting at Camp David scheduled Wednesday May 27 (WH official to CNBC).

Day 89 — TRUMP 'FINISH THE JOB' AT WHITE HOUSE CABINET MEETING; NEW US AIRSTRIKE ON A SOUTHERN-IRAN MILITARY SITE + MULTIPLE DRONE INTERCEPTS; IRAN FIRES BALLISTIC MISSILE AT KUWAIT (10:17 PM ET, INTERCEPTED) — CENTCOM: 'EGREGIOUS CEASEFIRE VIOLATION'; S&P 2ND STRAIGHT RECORD 7,520.36 (+0.02%), DOW RECORD 50,644.28; JULY WTI SETTLES $88.68 (-5.55%, 5-WEEK LOW) ON DEAL OPTIMISM, BRENT ~$93.91; LEBANON +~31 ON ONE OF THE HEAVIEST ISRAELI BOMBING DAYS IN WEEKS, ISRAEL ORDERS FORCED DISPLACEMENT OF ALL SOUTH LEBANON: Trump (Cabinet meeting): 'We're not satisfied with it, but we will be. Either that, or we'll have to just finish the job'; ruled out sanctions relief for HEU ('Not sanctions relief, no') and said he won't rush ('I don't care about the midterms'). US carried out a new airstrike on a southern-Iran military site threatening US forces and commercial Hormuz traffic + intercepted multiple Iranian drones (US official via ABC/CNN). At 10:17 p.m. ET Iran fired a ballistic missile at Kuwait, intercepted by Kuwaiti forces; CENTCOM: 'This egregious ceasefire violation… occurred hours after Iranian forces launched five one-way attack drones that posed a clear threat in and near the Strait of Hormuz.' IRGC claimed it struck a US air base in Kuwait. MARKETS: S&P 500 7,520.36 (+0.02%) record close; Dow 50,644.28 record; Nasdaq 26,674.73; July WTI settled $88.68 (-5.55%), Brent ~$93.91 — CNBC: oil 'betting on a swift end.' Lebanese cumulative 3,213 (MoH May 26) / 3,269 (CNN May 27). LMT $531.14. Iran MoH toll held at 3,468 (no new figure since May 20).

Day 90 — TENTATIVE 60-DAY US-IRAN MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS (UNSIGNED; TRUMP APPROVAL PENDING; IRAN/TASNIM DENIES FINALIZATION); OVERNIGHT US STRIKE ON IRGC DRONE GROUND-CONTROL STATION AT BANDAR ABBAS + 4-5 DRONE SHOOTDOWNS NEAR HORMUZ; IRGC WARNING SHOTS AT 4 HORMUZ VESSELS; S&P 3RD STRAIGHT RECORD 7,563.63 (+0.58%); OIL REBOUNDS ~2.5% (BRENT ~$96.63, WTI >$91); AAA GAS $4.426; SHUWAYFAT STRIKE KILLS A WOMAN, HER BABY, AND A SYRIAN CHILD: Axios reported US and Iranian negotiators reached a tentative 60-day MOU — unrestricted Hormuz shipping (no tolls/harassment), Iran de-mines within 30 days, US blockade lifted proportionally, Iran pledges no nuclear weapon, US to discuss sanctions relief + frozen assets — but it needs Trump's approval and Iran had NOT confirmed; Tasnim denied finalization. VP Vance: 'making some progress' but 'not there yet.' Treasury Sec. Bessent declined to confirm details, threatened Oman with sanctions over Hormuz tolls. KINETIC: overnight US shot down 4-5 Iranian attack drones near Hormuz + struck an IRGC drone ground-control station at Bandar Abbas; IRGC Navy fired warning shots at 4 vessels attempting unauthorized transit. MARKETS: S&P 500 7,563.63 (+0.58%) record; Nasdaq 26,917.47 (+0.91%); Dow ~50,669; Brent rebounded ~2.48% toward ~$96.63, WTI back above $91 — still tracking a 2nd straight weekly decline; AAA gas eased to $4.426; LMT $537.21; UBS raised its Brent forecast to $105. LEBANON: Shuwayfat strike (south of Beirut) killed a woman, her baby daughter, and a Syrian child (+3), wounded 15; Sidon apartment-building strike; IDF claimed 135 Hezbollah targets in 24h. Israeli reservist Sgt. Rotem Yanai killed by a Hezbollah drone. COST: Pentagon official held ~$29B (Hurst); Bilmes ~$2B/day, ~$1T projected lifetime; AEI ~$260/household.

Day 91 — TENTATIVE 60-DAY CEASEFIRE EXTENSION REACHED; TRUMP IN SITUATION ROOM FOR 'FINAL DETERMINATION'; BLOCKADE TO BE LIFTED; OIL FALLS ~2%; DOW TOPS 51,000 FOR FIRST TIME. US-Iran negotiators agreed a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension (pending Trump sign-off); Iran says no deal yet and refuses nuclear talks. Trump in the White House Situation Room for a 'final determination'; posted demands (Iran never to have a nuclear weapon; Hormuz immediately open with no tolls; mines removed/detonated; enriched 'nuclear dust' destroyed with IAEA; 'no money will be exchanged, until further notice') and announced the US naval blockade 'will now be lifted' and stranded ships 'may start the process of heading home.' Iran foreign ministry: 'we are focused on ending the war, and there are no negotiations on the nuclear issue.' Speaker/negotiator Ghalibaf: 'we have no trust in guarantees or words — only actions are the measure.' MARKETS: S&P 500 7,580.08 (+0.22%) — 4th straight record + 9th straight weekly gain, longest since 2023; Dow ~51,037 (+0.73%) — first close above 51,000 ever; Nasdaq ~26,972 (+0.26%); Russell 2000 ~2,919 (-0.60%); VIX 15.41. OIL FELL ~2% at 5-6 week lows on deal news — Brent $91.82 (-0.95%), WTI ~$87.36 (-1.73%); Brent ended May -17%, worst month since 2020. AAA gas $4.391 — biggest one-day drop since Nov 22, 2008. Defense names (RTX/LMT/NOC) under pressure; ITA -12% since early March. CENTCOM blockade tally as of May 29: 115 commercial vessels redirected (vs 100 May 23), 4 disabled. history.note: US-Iran negotiators agreed a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension (pending Trump sign-off); Iran says no deal yet and refuses nuclear talks. Dow tops 51,000 for first time.

history.headline: Day 92 (May 30, Saturday) — NO SIGNED MOU; TRUMP 'TOUGHENED' TERMS (NYT) / 'SEVERAL AMENDMENTS' (AXIOS); IRAN (BAGHAEI, GHALIBAF) SAYS NO AGREEMENT EXISTS; HEGSETH AT SHANGRI-LA DIALOGUE — TRUMP $1.5T DEFENSE PLAN, 3.5% GDP ALLIED ASK; OMAN MARITIME SECURITY CENTRE REPORTS SUSPECTED FLOATING MINE IN HORMUZ (NOT US-CONFIRMED); BLOOMBERG DISCLOSES MAY 27 KUWAIT FALLOUT: ~5 US WIA + 2 MQ-9 REAPERS HIT BY DEBRIS; +1 IDF KIA IN SOUTHERN LEBANON. TRUMP TELLS FOX NEWS HE IS 'IN NO HURRY' AND THE ONLY GUARANTEE HE REQUIRES IS 'NO NUCLEAR WEAPONS'; IRAN REASSERTS HORMUZ CONTROL VIA KHATAM AL-ANBIYA ORDER (ALL VESSELS TO USE DESIGNATED ROUTES + OBTAIN IRGC NAVY AUTHORIZATION); IRGC CLAIMS DOWNING A US DRONE (UNVERIFIED); IRAN UNVEILS '27 RAJAB' NAVAL ATTACK CRAFT IN TEHRAN; US DISABLES GAMBIA-FLAGGED SHIP (BLOCKADE TALLY +1, NOW 5); IRAN STATE MEDIA $12BN FROZEN-ASSET CLAIM CALLED 'FABRICATION' BY WH; CONGRESS ADVANCES US-ISRAELI MILITARY INTEGRATION. history.headline: Day 94 (June 1, Monday) — CEASEFIRE STRAINED: IRAN SUSPENDS INDIRECT TALKS. IRGC-linked Tasnim says Tehran is 'opening other fronts' (citing Israeli actions in Lebanon + US ceasefire violations) and suspends document exchange; FM spokesman Baqaei: a Lebanon ceasefire is 'an essential condition for any deal.' Trump counters ('continuing, at a rapid pace') and tells CNBC's Eamon Javers 'I really don't care. I couldn't care less.' KUWAIT intercepts 'hostile' Iranian missile/drone fire (FM holds Iran 'fully responsible'); IRGC claims it struck 'the air base from which the attack originated' (UNVERIFIED). MARKETS: oil SURGES on conflict fears — Brent settles $94.98 (+4.24%), WTI $92.54 (+5.93%); S&P 500 RECORD 7,599.96 (+0.26%), Nasdaq 27,086.81 (+0.42%), Dow 51,078.88 (+0.09%) — all records on a tech rally (Nvidia +6%). history.note: Iran suspends indirect talks (Tasnim, 'opening other fronts'); Trump 'rapid pace'; Kuwait intercepts Iranian missile/drone fire, IRGC claims retaliatory strike (base UNVERIFIED); oil surges (Brent $94.98 +4.24%, WTI $92.54 +5.93%); S&P record 7,599.96; gas $4.322; ITEP $46.5B/$347.72 per household.

history.headline: Day 95 (June 2, Tuesday) — TALKS 'BACK ON TRACK': TRUMP TELLS ABC NEWS A DEAL TO REOPEN HORMUZ + EXTEND THE CEASEFIRE IS REACHABLE 'OVER THE NEXT WEEK'; a regional source tells CNN negotiations are 'back on track' — a partial walk-back of June 1's suspension. history.note: Talks 'back on track' (CNN regional source); Trump tells ABC a deal is reachable 'over the next week'; Iran's internet partially restored; Pars restores 3 offshore platforms; Lebanon 3,433/10,395 (June 2); oil near $95; equities near records.

history.headline: Day 96 (June 3, Wednesday) — KINETIC EXCHANGES INTENSIFY; HOUSE REBUKES TRUMP 215-208: an Iranian drone/missile strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one Indian national and wounded 63+ (a terminal was briefly closed); the US struck an Iranian oil tanker off Qeshm; Iran's missiles/drones at Kuwait and Bahrain were largely intercepted. The US House passed an Iran war-powers resolution 215-208 — the first successful such vote (four Republicans crossed; 60% public disapproval per PBS/NPR/Marist). MARKETS: oil climbed toward $100 (Brent ~$97.98, +2.1%) and the S&P 500 snapped a nine-day record-setting win streak (-0.74%; Dow -1.21%, Nasdaq -0.89%); defense (LMT +14.9% YTD) and oil majors outperformed. Ceasefire 'tested' but holding; the 60-day extension MoU remains unsigned. Daily burn ~$150M. US KIA 13. Lebanon ~3,473 killed (+5 incl. a child).
history.note: Kuwait airport drone/missile strike kills 1 (Indian national), 63+ wounded; US strikes an Iranian tanker off Qeshm; House passes war-powers resolution 215-208; oil nears $100; S&P snaps a nine-day win streak (-0.74%); Lebanon ~3,473 (+5).

history.headline: Day 97 (June 4, Thursday) — DE-ESCALATION TONE AS A US-MEDIATED ISRAEL-LEBANON CEASEFIRE IS ANNOUNCED (IMMEDIATELY TESTED): CENTCOM intercepted an additional wave of Iranian drones aimed at US forces in Kuwait (all intercepted, no US casualties); Iran's navy claimed it struck a US CENTCOM facility — CENTCOM denied it. No new US strike on Iranian territory. DIPLOMACY: Iran's FM Araghchi said talks made 'no progress' but channels stay open; Hezbollah rejected the Lebanon ceasefire terms (AP); Treasury Secretary Bessent testified to the House. MARKETS: oil eased (Brent ~$96.70 −1.1%, WTI ~$95.17) on ceasefire hopes; the S&P 500 rebounded +0.41% to 7,584.31 and the Dow hit a record 51,561.93 (+1.73%) on a value rotation out of chips (Nasdaq −0.09%); AAA gas eased to $4.241. US weekly jobless claims hit their highest since the war began. Daily burn ~$110M. US KIA 13; tracked-category casualties unchanged.
history.note: US-mediated Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announced (immediately tested; Hezbollah rejects terms); CENTCOM intercepts an additional Iranian drone wave at Kuwait (no US losses); Iran navy's US-facility strike claim denied; oil eases (Brent ~$96.70), S&P +0.41% to 7,584.31, Dow record 51,561.93; gas $4.241; US jobless claims at a war-high.

history.headline: Day 98 (June 5, Friday) — US-IRAN TRADE FIRE OVER HORMUZ (4 IRGC DRONES DOWNED, US RADAR STRIKES AT QESHM/GORUK, IRANIAN MISSILE SALVOS AT KUWAIT/BAHRAIN ALL INTERCEPTED); WALL STREET'S WORST DAY SINCE OCTOBER ON A CHIP-LED ROUT, NOT A WAR SHOCK. CENTCOM downed 4 IRGC drones threatening Hormuz shipping and struck Iranian coastal radar at Qeshm Island and Goruk; Iran fired 7 ballistic missiles + drones at US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain — all intercepted, zero casualties. MARKETS: S&P 500 -2.64% to 7,383.74 (worst since Oct 10, 2025), Nasdaq -4.18% to 25,709.43, Dow -1.35% to 50,866.78 — a chip-led tech rout (Broadcom/Nvidia/Micron) + hot May jobs (+172,000), not a direct war shock; Brent $93.09 (-2.04%), WTI $90.54 (-2.69%); gas ~$4.21. Daily burn ~$170M (heaviest of the skirmish phase).
history.note: US-Iran Hormuz exchange (4 drones downed, US radar strikes at Qeshm/Goruk, 7 Iranian ballistic missiles + drones at Kuwait/Bahrain all intercepted, zero casualties); S&P -2.64% to 7,383.74 on a chip-led rout + hot jobs, not a war shock; Brent $93.09, WTI $90.54; gas ~$4.21.

history.headline: Day 99 (June 6, Saturday) — IDF STRIKE KILLS 3 LEBANESE ARMY SOLDIERS (INCL. A BRIGADIER GENERAL) NEAR KFAR TEBNIT; TRUMP SAYS THE WAR IS 'LARGELY FINISHED ... ONE WAY OR THE OTHER'; US DOWNS 2 MORE IRANIAN DRONES NEAR HORMUZ (TWO-DAY TOTAL 6); MARKETS CLOSED (WEEKEND). The Lebanese cumulative is reported at 3,593+ (LB Health Ministry / Wikipedia, as of June 6). US (Treasury) signals frozen Iranian assets may fund Gulf-ally reconstruction. Markets closed — Friday June 5 closes carry (S&P 7,383.74; Brent $93.09; WTI $90.54); AAA gas ~$4.19. Daily burn ~$110M.
history.note: IDF strike kills 3 LAF soldiers (incl. a brigadier general) near Kfar Tebnit; Trump: war 'largely finished ... one way or the other'; US downs 2 more drones near Hormuz; Lebanon 3,593+; markets closed (weekend).

history.headline: Day 100 (June 7, Sunday) — DAY 100: THE WAR HAS SETTLED INTO A BLOCKADE-PLUS-SKIRMISH EQUILIBRIUM CENTERED ON THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ. The June 5-6 cycle (IRGC drone harassment, US coastal-radar strikes, intercepted Iranian missile salvos, zero casualties) is the new tempo; Trump (June 6) called the war 'largely finished ... one way or the other.' Iran's May oil exports collapsed ~93% to 2.01M barrels (UANI) — the blockade, not airstrikes, is now Washington's primary lever. Oil eased to $93.09 Brent / $90.54 WTI; gas eased to $4.174; the S&P's June 5 -2.64% drop was a chip/rates move, not a war shock (still +7.9% YTD). Markets closed (weekend); Friday closes carry. Daily burn ~$95M (weekend floor); cumulative official ~$29B (Pentagon, frozen since May 12).
history.note: Day 100: blockade-plus-skirmish equilibrium; Trump says war 'largely finished'; Iran May oil exports -93% (UANI); oil $93.09/$90.54, gas $4.174; markets decoupled (S&P June 5 drop was tech/rates, +7.9% YTD); cumulative official ~$29B.

history.headline: Day 101 (June 8, Monday) — The fragile post-ceasefire equilibrium shattered. Overnight June 7-8 Iran fired ~30 ballistic missiles at Israel — its first direct strike on Israeli soil since the April ceasefire — retaliating for Israel's June 7 strike on Beirut's Dahieh suburb, killing Israeli civilians across Beit Shemesh, Haifa and Ramat Gan. Defying Trump's calls for restraint, Israel struck back at air-defense and missile-material targets in Tehran, Isfahan, Tabriz and a Mahshahr petrochemical complex. Both sides then announced a mutual suspension after Trump publicly called for an 'immediate CEASEFIRE'; he told a South Carolina tele-rally the US would declare 'total victory' within two weeks. Brent spiked above $97 (+5% intraday) before settling at $94.25 on the suspension; equities recovered as chips rebounded (S&P +0.30%). Separately, a US F/A-18 from USS Abraham Lincoln disabled the Palau-flagged tanker M/T Marivex — the 7th vessel disabled under the blockade.
history.note: First direct Iran-Israel exchange since April; mutual suspension brokered by Trump; oil spikes then eases.

history.headline: Day 102 (June 9, Tuesday) — A US Army AH-64 Apache was downed over the Strait of Hormuz (night June 8-9 local time); both pilots were rescued within ~2 hours by a US Navy Corsair uncrewed surface vessel of 5th Fleet's Task Force 59. Trump blamed an Iranian attack drone and vowed to respond 'of necessity.' CENTCOM launched self-defense strikes beginning 5pm ET, concluding within four hours, hitting Iranian air-defense, ground-control and surveillance-radar sites near the Strait with USAF and Navy fighter jets. Oil had fallen ~3% to a 7-week low (~$88 WTI) on the morning's truce optimism before the strikes; the S&P slipped 0.26% intraday and the strikes hit after the close. A US aircraft also disabled the Palau-flagged tanker M/T Settebello at 11:14pm — the 8th vessel disabled; 3 of 24 Indian crew went missing.
history.note: US Apache downed near Hormuz; US resumes direct strikes on Iran; 8th tanker disabled.

history.headline: Day 103 (June 10, Wednesday) — Iran retaliated for the US strikes early Wednesday: the IRGC launched drones at the US Fifth Fleet HQ in Bahrain and Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, and long-range ballistic missiles at Azraq (Muwaffaq Salti) Air Base in Jordan — Iran's deepest reach of the war (~1,000km from the Iranian coast). Jordan said it intercepted 5 missiles (debris only, no casualties); Bahrain and Kuwait also reported interceptions. The IRGC claimed 21 US targets struck and 4 destroyed including an F-35 hangar, plus downing an MQ-9 Reaper over Jam — all UNVERIFIED and disputed by US officials, who reported no US casualties or damage. Trump declared 'Iran is all talk and no action … they will have to pay the price!!!' US CPI printed at 4.2% year-over-year (highest since April 2023; energy +23.5%, gasoline +40.5%), while core CPI was a milder +0.2% m/m. Markets sold off hard: S&P 500 -1.62% to 7,266.99, Dow -1.87% (-953pts) to 49,918.78, Nasdaq -1.98% to 25,169.50; VIX surged ~11% (~22). WTI settled +2.07% at $90.03, Brent +1.8% at $93.10.
history.note: Iran hits Gulf bases (Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan); markets tumble; CPI tops 4%; ceasefire framework in crisis.

history.headline: Day 104 (June 11, Thursday) — On the evening of June 11, President Trump cancelled further strikes on Iran and claimed a 'great settlement' approved 'by all parties,' halting the land war; a final early-morning CENTCOM wave had hit Sirik, Minab, Bandar Abbas, Qeshm and Gorgan. Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya HQ declared the Strait of Hormuz fully closed to all vessels (the IRGC claimed strikes on two transiting ships; CENTCOM denied, saying the strait 'remains open'). Markets staged a relief rally — S&P 500 +1.75% to 7,394.30, Dow +1.86% to 50,848.75, Nasdaq +2.54% to 25,809.66 — and oil fell ~4% in extended trade (Brent ~$89, WTI ~$86.50). The ECB raised rates a quarter-point to 2.25%, the first major central bank to respond to the Iran energy shock. No US strikes on Iranian territory occurred after June 11.
history.note: Trump cancels further strikes; land war stops; Hormuz declared closed; relief rally.

history.headline: Day 105 (June 12, Friday) — Diplomacy accelerated toward a deal: Pakistan PM Sharif announced a 'final, agreed upon text' while VP Vance told CBS endorsement was 'still TBD' and Treasury Secretary Bessent said a deal could come 'this weekend or Monday.' Stocks extended gains (S&P 500 +0.50% to 7,431.46; Dow +0.70% to 51,202.26; Nasdaq +0.31% to 25,888.84) and oil hit an eight-week low (Brent $87.33 −3.4%, WTI $84.88 −3.2%). SpaceX (SPCX) debuted on the Nasdaq at $160.95 (+19.22% from its $135 IPO price), raising $75B at a ~$1.75T valuation — the largest IPO in history, eclipsing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record. June 12-15 saw only Hormuz drone interceptions, no strikes on Iran.
history.note: Deal text nears; stocks rise; oil at 8-week low; SpaceX IPO is largest ever.

history.headline: Day 106 (June 13, Saturday) — FM Araghchi said the US-Iran deal could be signed 'within days,' executed digitally; the White House named VP Vance for a Geneva ceremony and four USAF C-17s reportedly moved to Europe. The US and Iran offered conflicting accounts of terms — the US describing full nuclear dismantlement, Iran's Mehr 14-point draft saying 'no new nuclear commitments.' Markets were closed for the weekend (Friday closes carry). The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health bulletin reached 3,756 killed / 11,632 wounded.
history.note: Signing 'within days'; conflicting term accounts; markets closed; Lebanon toll 3,756.

history.headline: Day 107 (June 14, Sunday) — Trump declared the US-Iran deal 'now complete,' posting that he authorizes 'the toll free opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and… the immediate removal of the United States Naval blockade,' with formal signing set for June 19 in Switzerland (Vance and envoy Witkoff for the US). Israel struck Beirut's Ghobeiri suburb (3 killed, 16 wounded); Trump said it 'should not have happened.' Iran's FM disputed a Sunday signing and Fars called a June 14 Geneva signing 'completely baseless.' The Lebanese MoPH cumulative rose to 3,783 killed / 11,699 wounded. Markets closed (weekend).
history.note: Trump declares deal complete; Hormuz reopening + blockade removal authorized; Beirut strike; Lebanon 3,783.

history.headline: Day 108 (June 15, Monday) — At the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France, Trump said the US-Iran deal was 'all signed' (a senior official confirmed Trump and VP Vance signed the MOU digitally); he said the Strait of Hormuz is 'partially open' now and will be 'completely open' and 'toll free' by Friday. Core terms: toll-free Hormuz, the naval blockade lifted, Iran clearing mines within 30 days, ~$24-25B in frozen Iranian assets released, a 60-day nuclear-talks window, and hostilities ending 'on all fronts, including Lebanon.' Iran's Deputy FM Gharibabadi said the strait closure continues until the deal is formally signed (June 19). Markets hit records on the peace: S&P 500 +1.65% to 7,554.29, Dow +0.92% to a record 51,671.03, Nasdaq +3.07% to 26,683.94, VIX 16.20; Brent fell 4.76% to $83.17 and WTI 4.87% to $80.75 — the lowest since March 4.
history.note: Deal 'all signed'; toll-free Hormuz + blockade removal; markets at records; oil at 3-month lows.

history.headline: Day 110 (June 17, Wednesday) — Two days before the June 19 signing in Switzerland (the Burgenstock complex over Lake Lucerne), the 14-point US-Iran MOU text was released (Bloomberg/NBC/Time): an end to the war on all fronts including Lebanon, a $300B reconstruction fund, sanctions waivers, on-site downblending of Iran's ~440kg of 60% HEU under IAEA, and Hormuz traffic restored to pre-war volume within 30 days. Oil hit a three-month low — Brent settled $78.96 (first sub-$80 close since March, -5%) and WTI $76.05 (-5.8%) on June 16 — as the S&P 500 slipped 0.57% to 7,511.35 even as the Dow set another record. Physical reality lagged the politics: only ~7 ships have transited Hormuz since the June 14 deal with 550+ stranded. The live spoiler is Lebanon, where Israeli strikes killed 4 on June 17 (at least 14 on June 16); Trump said Netanyahu must be 'more responsible' while warning he would go 'back to dropping bombs' if Iran 'misbehaves,' and Iran said Israel has violated the Lebanon truce 84 times since the MOU. The Senate rejected a war-powers resolution 47-48.
history.note: Two days before the Switzerland signing; 14-point MOU text released; Hormuz still effectively closed (~7 ships since the deal); Israel kills 4 in Lebanon, Trump rebukes Netanyahu; oil at 3-month lows.

history.headline: Day 113 (June 20, Saturday) — The Iran war is effectively over: the 14-point US-Iran MOU was signed June 17 (Trump at the Palace of Versailles, Pezeshkian in Tehran) and CENTCOM lifted the naval blockade June 18, reopening the Strait of Hormuz toll-free, with >12.5M barrels transiting Wednesday night. But the June 19 Switzerland follow-on ceremony was cancelled, and Lebanon became the residual hot front: at least 47 were killed June 19 (the deadliest post-MOU day) and four IDF soldiers died before a US/Qatar/Iran-mediated Israel-Hezbollah truce was renewed (~9am ET), then strained by June 20 strikes (≥7 killed, incl. 2 children) and a 50+ projectile barrage. Markets priced in peace — Brent ~$80.57 and WTI ~$77.54 (June 19), the S&P 500 at 7,500.58 (June 18 close; markets closed June 19 for Juneteenth), and AAA gas $3.973, the first sustained sub-$4.00 since late March — while Moody's pegged the cumulative US consumer/taxpayer cost at ~$132B. Both carriers (Lincoln, Bush) remain on station in the Arabian Sea; no withdrawal has been ordered.
history.note: War effectively over on the Iran front: MOU signed June 17, blockade lifted June 18, Hormuz reopened toll-free. June 19 Switzerland ceremony cancelled; Lebanon the residual hot front (≥47 killed June 19, 4 IDF KIA, truce renewed then strained June 20). Markets priced in peace; carriers remain on station.

history.headline: Day 118 (June 25, Thursday) — The oil war-risk premium has collapsed: Brent settled $73.74 and WTI $70.34 (June 24), both at/near pre-war levels and down ~40% from the wartime peak, dragging the AAA national gas average to $3.928 (a sixth straight weekly drop). The OFAC 60-day sanctions waiver (General License X), surging Hormuz transits (~62 vessels June 24) and Brent's flip into bearish contango drove the slide; the S&P 500 eased 0.10% to 7,358.22 after a June 23 tech/chip selloff (Nasdaq -2.21%). CSIS pegged the total Epic Fury cost at ~$40B ($34B-$42B) as the White House requested an $87.6B supplemental ($67.15B DoD) and the Senate passed a historic 50-48 War Powers rebuke. But the ceasefire frayed on two seams: the IRGC reasserted permission-only Hormuz transit and struck the container ship Ever Lovely (the first ship attack since the June 18 reopening), and the fifth Israel-Lebanon round stalled with no signing. Carriers Lincoln and Bush remain on station in the Arabian Sea; no withdrawal has been ordered.
history.note: Oil hits a pre-war low (Brent $73.74); IRGC strikes the Ever Lovely in Hormuz; Senate passes a 50-48 war-powers rebuke; WH seeks an $87.6B supplemental. CSIS total ~$40B. The US-Iran direct front stayed quiet (no strikes since ~June 10-11) but Hormuz and Lebanon remained strained.

history.headline: Day 123 (June 30, Tuesday) — The ceasefire re-escalated then stood down: between June 25 and June 28 the US and Iran traded four days of kinetic strikes over Strait of Hormuz shipping — the first US strikes on Iranian soil since the June 17 MOU. After IRGC drones hit the M/V Ever Lovely (June 25) and the tanker M/T Kiku (June 27), CENTCOM struck 14 Iranian targets across June 26-27 (4 near Sirik, then 10 in and near the strait); Iran retaliated against Kuwait (2 ballistic missiles intercepted) and Bahrain (a Muharraq residential building hit, no deaths) on June 28, and a Qatari national was killed at sea by shrapnel. A senior US official announced a 'stand down for now' June 28-29 ('vessels can move freely'); Trump set Doha talks for June 30 (Iran unconfirmed). A US-brokered Israel-Lebanon framework was signed June 26. Markets decoupled from the shooting — Brent set fresh post-war lows (~$72 June 26) before firming to ~$74, and the Dow closed above 52,000 for the first time. Moody's pegs the cost to US consumers and taxpayers at ≥$132B. Carriers Lincoln and Bush held station in the Arabian Sea throughout; no surge or withdrawal.
history.note: Re-escalation June 25-28: four days of US-Iran strikes over Hormuz shipping (14 US targets June 26-27); Iran hit Kuwait & Bahrain June 28; stand-down June 28-29; Doha talks set for June 30 (Iran unconfirmed). Israel-Lebanon framework signed June 26. Oil ~$74, gas $3.847, Dow first close >52,000, Moody's cost ≥$132B. No new US casualties; no verified new Iranian deaths.

history.headline: Day 129 (July 6, Monday) — Combat froze; diplomacy advanced. The June 29 US-Iran stand-down held for the entire July 1-6 window — zero new kinetic exchanges between the US and Iran. Indirect technical talks in Doha (July 1-2, via Qatari and Pakistani mediators) concluded with 'positive progress': a mechanism to use part of the $6B in frozen, Qatar-held Iranian funds for goods purchases plus a violations-communications channel; talks resume ~July 11 after Ayatollah Khamenei's state funeral (July 4-9; main Tehran procession July 6). Oil and equities leaned toward peace — Brent closed $71.73 and WTI $68.44 (July 6) near pre-war lows after OPEC+ agreed July 5 to add 188,000 bpd in August, while the Dow set a record 52,900.07 (July 2) and topped 53,000 intraday July 6 and AAA gas fell to $3.804. The only new US casualty event was NON-COMBAT: a Navy MH-60S ditched in the Arabian Sea July 1, three of four aircrew recovered and one aircrewman lost (search suspended July 5; presumed dead, not yet KIA). Lebanon stayed the lone kinetic front — Israel struck 10 Hezbollah sites July 3 and the Lebanese toll rose to ~4,301. Carriers Lincoln and Bush held station in the Arabian Sea; no surge or withdrawal.
history.note: Stand-down held all six days (July 1-6): no new US-Iran strikes. Doha talks made 'positive progress' ($6B frozen-funds goods mechanism + violations channel), resume ~July 11 after Khamenei's funeral. Oil near pre-war lows (Brent $71.73 / WTI $68.44) after OPEC+ +188k bpd; Dow record 52,900 (Jul 2), >53,000 intraday Jul 6; gas $3.804. One non-combat US loss (MH-60S aircrewman off the Bush; presumed lost, not yet KIA). Lebanon toll ~4,301. No new Iranian deaths.

history.headline: Day 137 (July 14, Tuesday) — CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED; HORMUZ BLOCKADE REIMPOSED. Iran fired on 3 Hormuz-area tankers Jul 7; Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' Jul 8; CENTCOM ran five-plus strike waves against 300+ Iranian targets Jul 7-14, including the first US combat use of sea drones (3 Saronic Corsair USVs, Bandar Abbas Naval Base, Jul 12). Iran struck US-linked sites in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, Oman and Qatar, a Kuwaiti offshore oil rig, and 2 UAE tankers (1 Indian sailor killed). The US naval blockade of Iranian ports took effect Jul 14, 20:00 GMT; Trump announced then reversed a 20% Hormuz cargo fee within ~24h. Brent settled +9.59% at $83.30 (Jul 13, biggest daily % gain since May 2020); S&P 500 -0.79% to 7,515.34; AAA gas $3.872. Iranian window tolls conflict by source (Health Ministry 14/78 then 17/115; Army 8; IRGC 3) — kept separate, never summed; cumulative counter held at the frozen 3,468 MoH benchmark. Nasdaq/Dow levels and a post-escalation cumulative cost figure were not published — recorded as null, not estimated. Daily cost $500M/day = CSIS active-ops lower bound, FLAGGED for manual review.

Day 138 (July 15, Wednesday) — BLOCKADE ENFORCED: US disabled the empty tanker Belma with Hellfire missiles near Kharg Island, the first vessel disabled under the reimposed blockade; the IRGC threatened to halt all Middle East energy exports. Brent settled $84.95.

Day 139 (July 16, Thursday) — STRIKES CONTINUE; TRANSITS HIT 3-WEEK LOW: A 3rd straight US strike night hit southern Iran; 11th MEU Marines boarded the tanker Wen Yao and Hormuz transits fell to 8/day. S&P 500 −1.01% to 7,457.69; Brent $84.23.

Day 140 (July 17, Friday) — FIRST US COMBAT DEATHS SINCE MARCH: An Iranian ballistic-missile strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Jordan, killed 3 US soldiers (Feehan, Gonzales, Rampersad; 4 medevac'd). A 7th straight US strike night hit bridges, a tunnel and the Bonji desalination plant at Jask, cutting water to ~10,000; a strike in Erbil killed ≥9 at a Komala facility; a child was wounded by debris in Doha. Brent jumped to $88.10 (+4.6%).

Day 143 (July 20, Monday) — GAS TOPS $4; HOUTHIS DECLARE SAUDI BLOCKADE: The AAA national average hit $4.003/gal, first time above $4 in over a month; the Houthis declared a Red Sea blockade of Saudi Arabia. Mediators floated a 10-day ceasefire; Trump vowed Iran would pay 'many times over.' A 4th US soldier's Jul 18 Iraq death brings KIA to 17. S&P 500 −0.19% to 7,443.28; Brent $89.22.

Day 144 (July 21, Tuesday) — AOUN MEETS TRUMP; PICKAXE MOUNTAIN THREAT: Lebanese President Aoun met Trump, who said the US would strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site 'probably pretty soon'; Iran warned of NPT withdrawal. S&P 500 +0.89% to 7,509.20 (breaking a 3-day losing streak); Brent settled $91.01.

Day 145 (July 22, Wednesday) — HOUSE PASSES $95B BLUEPRINT; DOVER TRANSFER; SAUDI TANKERS HIT: The House adopted a Republican-only $95B budget blueprint (>$70B for the Iran war) 216-214, plus a Pentagon CR through Dec 4. Trump attended the Dover dignified transfer of four fallen. Houthis attacked the Saudi tankers Encelia and Layla in the Red Sea. S&P 500 −0.14% to 7,498.96; Brent settled $94.07.

Day 146 (July 23, Thursday) — 12TH STRAIGHT STRIKE NIGHT; BRENT NEARS $100: CENTCOM completed a 12th consecutive night of strikes; Iranian state media reported 2 killed at the Shalamcheh border crossing. Brent spiked toward $100 intraday (+6.4%), first time above $100 since late May; WTI ~$91.24. Rubio said Iran is 'not serious' about talks; Trump said the US would 'hold Iran responsible' for Houthi attacks. New cost figures: $37.5B direct US military (Hegseth); ~$71.1B consumer gas/diesel (Brown/Watson).

Day 150 (July 27, Monday) — MUTUAL STRIKE PAUSE HOLDS A THIRD DAY; OIL CRASHES ~9%: CENTCOM's 13-night campaign ended 9 p.m. ET Jul 23 and no US strikes followed Jul 24-27; Iran halted retaliation after its Jul 24 IRGC salvo. Mediators led by Qatar and Pakistan told AP they made 'significant' progress toward restoring the interim ceasefire, though an Al Jazeera source said Jul 26 there was 'not much progress yet'; Iran confirms no direct US talks. Brent settled $88.36 (-8.7%), the biggest one-day drop since Apr 8, off the $101.01 intraday high of Jul 23; WTI $82.61. Gas $4.110. S&P 7,413.18 (+0.02%) as the relief rally faded. Pentagon DCAS restored the toll to 18 killed / 624 wounded under a new split-category accounting. The war's geography widened even as its core cooled: Houthis struck Saudi Aramco at Jizan and Yanbu (Jul 25) and Ukraine struck an Iranian vessel in the Caspian (Jul 25). Trump warns strikes resume 'with greater force' if talks fail.

Day 157 (August 3, Monday) — TRUMP CALLS OFF 'BIGGEST ATTACK SINCE WWII,' ANNOUNCES IRAN TALKS; OIL SLUMPS ~6%: The fourth escalate-then-pause cycle since June ran its full course in seven days. Iran's IRGC broke a multi-day lull with an attempted surprise missile attack on US forces at 5:45 p.m. ET Jul 28 (all intercepted; Jordan downed five), and US and Saudi forces struck Iran-aligned groups in eastern Iraq the same day — the first public Saudi participation in US operations. CENTCOM answered with a 'heavy wave' completed 10 p.m. ET Jul 29 against dozens of IRGC targets; Iranian media reported a family of three killed on Qeshm Island and the IRGC named three personnel killed. Iran struck Jordan and Kuwait Jul 30 (1 killed in Kuwait); Saudi Arabia convened 40+ nations on a naval coalition; the IRGC claimed two Hormuz tanker strikes Jul 31 (UNVERIFIED — Kpler still logged two VLCCs exiting). Then Trump canceled a planned major strike on Iranian energy infrastructure late Aug 1, saying 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to' including the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT'; Iran's Mehr called it 'simply a new lie' Aug 2; Trump said Aug 3 that negotiations begin. Markets whipsawed on the diplomacy, not the fighting: Brent $90.74 Jul 29 → ~$83 Aug 3; WTI ~$79; S&P ~7,537 (+0.63%) after a first red July since 2014. Toll counters HELD — no cumulative revisions issued; US WIA 624 (DCAS via The Hill) against AP's 642 under a new 'Overseas Operations' category. Hormuz traffic still ~12/day. PROVISIONAL: Aug 3 oil and equity values are intraday.

Day 163 (August 9, Sunday) - HORMUZ TALKS GRIND ON AS IRAN HARDENS TERMS: The Aug 1-3 pause held a full week with no new US strikes on Iranian soil. Iran's SNSC issued formal preconditions Aug 8 (lift the blockade, withdraw US forces, permanently end the war, war-damage compensation); a UAE/ADNOC tanker was struck by an Iranian missile Aug 8 and left burning. Oman calls talks 'constructive' but warns the vessel attacks threaten them; CJCS Caine reportedly presses for an 'off-ramp.' US and Iran are passing messages via intermediaries. Markets closed the week at records (S&P 7,757.64, +3.6%) on Iran de-escalation and a soft jobs report; Brent fell ~7% on the week to ~$83.55.

Day 170 (August 16, Sunday) - TALKS STALL, TANKERS BURN, CARRIER LEAVES ASIA: The strike pause held a second full week (no US strikes on Iranian soil since ~Aug 1), but Hormuz stayed violent — Iran drone-struck two ADNOC tankers Aug 13 (no injuries; ADNOC ~15-17 vessels hit since Feb). Talks stalled: Trump vowed to make Hormuz 'US territory,' FM Araghchi said it 'cannot be seized with a tweet' and left resumption undecided; mediation widened to European players as Kushner toured the region. Bessent threatened 'economic isolation' of Iran; Hegseth floated an indefinite blockade. Oil rose ~5-6% on the week (Brent $88.52, WTI $82.40); the S&P hit a record 7,798.99 Thu before easing to 7,785.76 Fri (3rd weekly gain) on weak July retail sales. Israel killed at least 11 in south Lebanon Aug 15 (deadliest since June). The Navy pulled its last carrier from Asia — USS George Washington sailing to relieve the USS Lincoln (240+ days at sea).

Day 178 (August 24, Monday) - THE WAR GOES FINANCIAL: The US strike pause on Iranian territory reached its 24th night as Washington swapped ordnance for sanctions. Trump declared an 'ECONOMIC D-DAY' on Aug 19 and called the Strait of Hormuz 'American territory' on Aug 22; Treasury Secretary Bessent promised the 'toughest sanctions in history,' said there would 'likely' be no large-scale kinetic restart, and unveiled what he called the single greatest financial offensive ever on Aug 24. The 60-day MOU window expired Aug 17 with no deal. At sea, USS George Washington arrived in CENTCOM Aug 19 and relieved USS Abraham Lincoln, which departed after a record 241+ consecutive days at sea - leaving no US carrier in the Pacific. The bulk carrier Minoan Dignity was struck exiting Hormuz Aug 18, killing one crew member. Brent settled $94.39 (+~6% on the week) and the S&P fell 1.4%, snapping a three-week win streak.

us_kia.note: Day 178: HELD at 18. No US military death reported Aug 17-24.

The DCAS figure now combines Operation Epic Fury with the newer 'Overseas Operations' category. iranian_killed.label: Iranian killed (cumulative, tracked line)
iranian_killed.note: Day 178: HELD at 3,636 (HRANA total: 1,701 civilian including at least 254 children, 1,221 military, 714 unclassified). No new strike casualties in-window — the pause held. RANGE PUBLISHED WITH ATTRIBUTION, NOT MERGED: Iran's Foundation of Martyrs confirms 3,468; Al Jazeera's Aug 12 compilation at least 3,527; US/Israeli estimates 6,000+. Do not synthesize a single number.

Tracked separately and NOT counted as war dead: at least 901 people have been executed in Iran since January 2026, 28 of them in August (Abdorrahman Boroumand Center).

lebanese_killed.label: Lebanese killed (cumulative, all)
lebanese_killed.note: Day 178: 4,308 -> ~4,319. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported at least 4,300 killed since Mar 2 (Reuters, Aug 15); further deaths followed in the Aug 22 Nabatiyeh and south Lebanon strikes, which the Ministry has not itemised. The +11 is DERIVED from reconciling the revised cumulative and should be replaced when a dated figure is published. Lebanon is a parallel front, decoupled from the Iran strike pause.
lebanese_killed.tooltip: Lebanese Health Ministry cumulative since Mar 2. Israeli operations against Hezbollah continue independently of the Iran pause; strikes on Nabatiyeh and south Lebanon on Aug 22 reportedly left 'no house undamaged' at Bayt al-Sayyad, with phosphorus munitions reported (Lebanon NNA).

displaced.note: Day 178: HELD at 1,200,000 (Lebanon-weighted). No new quantified figure in-window. LIKELY UNDERCOUNT — Iran separately has roughly 3.2 million internally displaced (UNHCR), which this counter does not include. Flag rather than estimate.

flights_cancelled.note: Day 178: HELD at 8,000. No new figure reported in-window.

HRANA documents at least 254 children killed in Iran alone; AOAV counts at least 212 across nine countries from English-language incident tracking (176 Iran, 24 Lebanon, 10 Israel, 1 Iraq). These are differently-scoped counts, not competing totals. Treat 379 as a floor.
